evidence: evals/launch-readiness/evals.json and scripts/lib/launch-evals.mjs define and validate seven dimensions, four human authority actions, all five reopen triggers, disagreement review, and structured overrides for judged launch records.
scripts/record-holdout-eval.mjs binds holdouts to the exact candidate commit and prompt, requires context-separation attestations, and refuses acceptance with blockers or incomplete score floors.
scripts/run-composite-eval.mjs creates an accepted-for-review deterministic record with no decisionRecord and no criterion vector when commands pass.
scripts/lib/eval-contract.mjs validates the full decision record only inside the holdout branch even though evals/_shared/contract.json sets requireDecisionRecord true.
scripts/tests/eval-contract.test.mjs constructs accepted deterministic records without decisionRecord and uses two such records in the test that satisfies the composite review stop.
risks: The aggregate review protocol says every run preserves multidimensional governance, but accepted deterministic records are an intentional exception not disclosed by the policy language.
A command-only accepted status can exist without a local authority, disagreement, override, or unresolved-risk record, weakening the claim that a passing boolean cannot erase deliberation.
External human gates remain explicit, but that does not repair the per-run governance omission.
criterionResults.rationale: The holdout path is strong, but the composite evaluator's accepted deterministic path preserves only commands and external gates. That is the frozen score-3 condition: multidimensional governance exists but remains incomplete in a certifying path.

blockingFindings: The composite certifying path does not enforce its own every-run decision-governance promise: scripts/run-composite-eval.mjs can emit accepted-for-review deterministic records without decisionRecord or criterionResults, scripts/lib/eval-contract.mjs applies requireDecisionRecord only to holdouts, and scripts/tests/eval-contract.test.mjs treats decision-record-free deterministic records as valid inputs to the passing stop condition. Align the policy, runner, validator, and tests before PR-review acceptance.

Public claim boundaries can drift between the canonical citation registry and the separate proofs.ts layer without failing projection checks. The drift is already visible: /work/196-sunday-dinner attributes 2,783 meals directly to a protected ledger while omitting that it is the workbook's own summary and differs by 14 from the aggregate audit, and /resume plus /work/technical-operations omit CallNYC's required archived/unofficial framing. Make one canonical projection authority, or validate exact wording and guardrails across every authorized surface, then correct the affected projections.

summary: Revision required before pull-request review. The portfolio is exceptionally clear about role, emerging work, collective credit, and human release authority, but evidence wording can drift across parallel public-claim layers and the composite evaluator permits accepted deterministic records without the seven-dimension governance record its policy promises. Visual proof also remains mostly descriptive, though it meets the minimum rather than independently blocking review. This judgment does not grant or assess production approval.
